title: EDS Curriculum — schema-preserving streaming constrained-decode test suite
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Goal: build a reproducible, curriculum-driven test harness (EDS = Emission-Driven Schema curriculum) that stresses schema adherence for streaming responses under realistic production conditions. This ticket captures the design, test cases, and automation required to validate constrained-decoding + streaming + toolcall interleaving behavior across model variants and runtime knobs. The harness must: 1) evaluate strict JSON mode pass rate on a canonical prompt corpus, 2) exercise partial-chunk corruption and reassembly recovery, 3) validate fallback policies (model variant and truncated-json fallback) and observability hooks, and 4) produce deterministic nightly metrics for regressions. This is intentionally a focused test-suite to complement the large chaos/fuzz suites by targeting structured-output emission patterns in streamed scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical schema corpus (~480 prompts) yields >= 99% strict JSON-mode parse success across baseline models with KV-cache disabled
Under streaming with partial-chunk corruption (simulated piecewise truncation), the constrained decoder recovers valid JSON or emits a single, documented fallback sentinel in >= 95% of cases
Tool-call interleaving scenarios (tool annotation mid-stream) do not corrupt outer JSON envelope in >= 98% of runs; any corruptions must trigger the documented fallback and an audit log entry
Backoff and retry policies are exercised: when emission violates schema for repeated attempts, the runtime selects fallback model variant and records time-to-fallback metric < 150ms on average
CI integration: tests run in the nightly pipeline and produce a machine-readable report in the runtime-1.18 artifacts bucket and a dashboardable CSV
Test harness includes reproducible seeds and deterministic fixtures so failures can be triaged without flakiness
test_plan: Construct canonical prompt corpus: mix of short/long context, nested objects, arrays-of-objects, typed enums, and toolcall markers (~480 prompts)
Matrix: models {open-lm-7b, redwood-13b-compat}, modes {streaming, non-streaming}, kv_cache {on, off}, quant_profile {fp16, q4_0}
Simulate partial-chunk network: split token streams at random token boundaries and reassemble with missing chunk scenarios (single-chunk-loss, mid-stream-truncation, interleaved toolcall insertion)
Adversarial seed set: prompts intentionally close to schema boundaries (missing commas, ambiguous keys, large arrays) to validate constrained-decoder robustness
Run constrained-decoder with increasing constraint strength curriculum: strict -> relaxed -> sentinel-fallback and record pass/fail and failure modes
Collect telemetry: schema_pass_rate, fallback_count, avg_time_to_fallback_ms, corrupted_bytes_before_recovery, PR metrics linking failing prompt IDs to model/version/build
how_to_run: python infra/tests/eds_runner.py --corpus canonical.json --mode streaming --model redwood-13b-compat --kv-cache off --seed 42
Nightly CI: .ci/nightly-eds.yaml triggers infra/tests/eds_runner with matrix and uploads runtime artifact CSV

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Nightly flakiness due to randomness in temperature sampling. Mitigation: force deterministic sampling seeds for test runs and clamp sampling to top-k where needed
Risk: Overfitting test harness to a small corpus. Mitigation: maintain an evolving seed corpus and rotate in customer-derived prompts monthly
Risk: Telemetry volume from detailed token-level logs. Mitigation: sample 1% of runs for full token trace, otherwise capture summarized failure payloads
Risk: False confidence when fallback sentinel masks real output regressions. Mitigation: add a periodic smoke-run that disables sentinel fallback and surfaces raw corruption rates
